patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` adds the missing `DT_HASH` chain bound check before the `si = get_te32(&chains[si])` backedge. On the original testcase the fixed build reaches the same guard state with `chain_index_in_bounds=0` and suppresses the protected `chain_reload` event, so the AddressSanitizer crash disappears. The adjacent 12-byte padding perturbation then makes the same backedge read in-bounds (`chain_index_in_bounds=1`) and executes the protected event genuinely on the fixed side.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: Source. Project code materializes the attacker-controlled ELF bytes into `file_image`; the later `PT_DYNAMIC`, `DT_SYMTAB`, and malformed `DT_HASH` state are all read from this buffer.

Root cause corresponding to the staged patch. Vulnerable code reloads the next `DT_HASH` chain index from `chains[si]` without first proving that `si` still indexes an in-bounds chain word; the fix adds an EOF-based guard before this backedge read.

Crash sink. The unchecked `chains[3]` pointer from `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup()` reaches this helper through `get_te32()` and `LEPolicy::get32()`, and the inline 4-byte copy performs the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-buffer-overflow read.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable backedge reload, the 4-byte read extent for `get_te32(&chains[si])` already crosses the end of `file_image`, so the loop asks the endian helper chain to read past the heap allocation.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `chain_reload_guard.chain_read_end_ptr > chain_reload_guard.file_end_ptr` at the selected backedge event.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records equal pointer values at `chain_reload.chain_word_ptr` and the immediately following `hash_sink.read_arg_ptr`.
